reviewer: Codex research agent, delegated researcher and verifier
scope: Twelve individually researched Arlington candidates with source-backed roles. No blanket approval of the national queue. No photos. Year-only dates retained where day precision has not completed review. Current actual interments distinguished from former burials and memorials. Await independent audit before release.

candidates.name: Dashiell Hammett
candidates.biography: Dashiell Hammett helped define hard-boiled detective fiction with novels including The Maltese Falcon and The Thin Man. Before becoming a writer, he worked as a detective. He also served in the Army during both world wars.
candidates.why_interesting: His detective work preceded the fictional investigations that made him famous.

burial_evidence.notes: The author is listed at Section 12, Grave 508. Years verified; exact dates withheld. Writing about crime does not justify a crime tag. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Maureen O'Hara
candidates.short_description: Irish-born film star and airline executive.
candidates.biography: Maureen O'Hara starred in films including Miracle on 34th Street and The Quiet Man. Beyond acting, she later led Antilles Air Boats. She is buried with her husband Charles Blair at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: Her career extended beyond Hollywood into running an airline.

burial_evidence.notes: Academy biography confirms birth and film career. Arlington identifies Maureen FitzSimons Blair at Section 2, Grave 4966, and her airline presidency. Death year verified; exact death date withheld. Her husband's service does not imply a military career for her. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Ludwig Bemelmans
candidates.short_description: Author and illustrator of the Madeline books.
candidates.biography: Ludwig Bemelmans created the Madeline children's books and worked as an illustrator and painter. An Army veteran, he also wrote about his service. His grave is at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: His creative work crossed children's literature, illustration, and painting.

burial_evidence.notes: Author-illustrator listed at Section 43, Grave 2618. Years and creative/military roles verified; exact dates withheld. Individual identity matched to the local article and lifetime. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Albert B. Sabin
candidates.short_description: Medical researcher who developed the oral polio vaccine.
candidates.biography: Albert B. Sabin helped develop the oral polio vaccine, which became available in 1961. His medical research also included work for the Army during World War II. He and his wife Heloisa are buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: His vaccine could be given by mouth rather than injection.

burial_evidence.notes: Sabin Vaccine Institute confirms exact dates, research and actual burial. Arlington lists Section 3, Grave 1885-RH and explicitly identifies the oral-vaccine invention and Army service. Q164790 matches Albert Bruce Sabin, not similarly named candidates. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Michael Ellis DeBakey
candidates.short_description: Cardiovascular surgeon, medical inventor, and Army veteran.
candidates.biography: Michael Ellis DeBakey advanced cardiovascular surgery and developed medical devices, including a roller pump used in heart-lung machines. His military medical work contributed to mobile surgical care. He is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: His innovations linked surgical devices with the organization of military care.

burial_evidence.notes: VA biography confirms exact dates and surgeon/inventor/veteran identity. Arlington lists Section 34, Grave 399-A and the pump and military surgical-hospital work. Scientific and invention tags reflect medical research and devices, not merely medical practice. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Jane Delano
candidates.short_description: Founder of the American Red Cross Nursing Service.
candidates.biography: Jane Delano built the American Red Cross Nursing Service and served as superintendent of the Army Nurse Corps. She organized nursing support for military and civilian needs. After dying in France in 1919, she was reinterred at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: Her organizing work helped prepare nursing services for wartime demand.

burial_evidence.notes: Red Cross institutional history supports nursing leadership; its April 26, 2019 Jane A. Delano article gives exact dates: https://www.redcrosschat.org/2019/04/26/jane-a-delano-pioneer-of-the-modern-nursing-profession/. Arlington confirms reinterment in Section 21, Grave 6. The separate Red Cross Square memorial is not her burial. Military tag follows Army Nurse Corps leadership, not a claim of combat service. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
candidates.short_description: Supreme Court justice and advocate for gender equality.
candidates.biography: Ruth Bader Ginsburg served on the U.S. Supreme Court from 1993 until her death in 2020. Before joining the bench, she taught law and helped lead the ACLU's Women's Rights Project. She is buried beside her husband Martin at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: She argued for equal rights before becoming a justice herself.

burial_evidence.notes: FJC confirms exact dates and judicial service. Arlington confirms Section 5, Grave 7016-1, actual burial beside Martin and women's-rights legal work. Government/politics and civil-rights tags follow documented public work; husband's Army service is not transferred to her. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Matthew Henson
candidates.biography: Matthew Henson accompanied Robert Peary on Arctic expeditions and published an account of his experiences in 1912. Recognition for his work grew later in his life. Originally buried in New York, he and his wife were reinterred at Arlington in 1988.
candidates.why_interesting: His final resting place changed decades after his death.

burial_evidence.notes: Dedicated Arlington page confirms April 6, 1988 actual reinterment; general Explorers page gives Section 8, Grave S-15-1. Its 1886 birth typo is rejected in favor of dedicated page1866 and Maryland State Archives tablet transcription. Independent auditor verified both exact dates at https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc5700/sc5774/000000/000011/000000/000006/pdf/sc5774-11-6.pdf. No unqualified first-to-the-Pole claim or military tag is inferred. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: John Wesley Powell
candidates.short_description: Geologist, Colorado River explorer, and Civil War veteran.
candidates.biography: John Wesley Powell led a landmark Colorado River expedition through the Grand Canyon in 1869. A Civil War veteran who lost an arm at Shiloh, he later directed the U.S. Geological Survey. He is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: His field expeditions preceded his leadership of a national scientific agency.

burial_evidence.notes: USGS biography confirms scientific leadership, expedition and military service. Arlington identifies Section 1, Grave 408. Independent auditor verified exact dates in Arlington's Army Walking Tour: https://education.arlingtoncemetery.mil/Portals/2/Army%20Walking%20Tour.pdf. No first-human exploration claim; the landscape was already known to Indigenous peoples. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: George Westinghouse
candidates.short_description: Inventor and industrialist associated with railway air brakes and electric power.
candidates.biography: George Westinghouse developed inventions that changed railway safety and electrical power. His businesses helped expand the use of alternating current, while his air brake became an important railway innovation. A Civil War veteran, he is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: His inventions reached both railway networks and electrical systems.

burial_evidence.notes: Library of Congress biographical essay supplies exact dates and invention/business record. Arlington identifies Section 2, Grave 3418 and Army/Navy service. Local QID and article identify the industrialist. No claim that he alone invented alternating current. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Hyman G. Rickover
candidates.short_description: Admiral who led the development of the U.S. nuclear Navy.
candidates.biography: Hyman G. Rickover directed the Navy's nuclear-propulsion program for decades, helping bring nuclear-powered submarines into service. His long naval career made him a central figure in the development of the modern submarine fleet. He is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: His career helped change how submarines were powered.

burial_evidence.notes: Naval History and Heritage Command supplies exact dates and program leadership. Arlington identifies Section 5, Grave 7000. Military and history tags are supported; engineering management does not automatically establish an inventor or scientist tag. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.

candidates.name: Elizebeth Smith Friedman
candidates.short_description: Codebreaker and writer who investigated encrypted smuggling communications.
candidates.biography: Elizebeth Smith Friedman used cryptanalysis to investigate coded communications for U.S. government agencies. Her work included cases involving international smugglers. She also collaborated with her husband William on a study of alleged Shakespeare ciphers. They are buried together at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: Her language skills became tools for decoding secret messages.

burial_evidence.notes: NSA confirms death date,1892 birth year and codebreaking/writing career. Independent auditor verified full birth date in Arlington's Coast Guard Walking Tour: https://education.arlingtoncemetery.mil/Portals/2/Coast%20Guard%20Walking%20Tour.pdf. Arlington confirms shared burial, Section 8, Grave 6379-A. Civilian work with military agencies is not itself a military commission; no military or crime tag inferred. Exact QID, linked article and lifetime checked; no existing-public flag or prior-wave duplicate. Coordinates are cemetery-level, not exact grave or entrance pins.
